items.title: 207 stranded as bad weather diverts China flight to Terengganu
items.summary: KUALA NERUS: A total of 207 passengers and crew members of Qingdao Airlines flight QW907 from China were stranded at Sultan Mahmud Airport (LTSM) yesterday afternoon due to bad weather. Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the Airbus A321neo aircraft was scheduled to land at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) but diverted to LTSM after circling for more than an hour in inclement weather. He said all passengers were temporarily accommodated at three hotels in Kuala Terengganu and Kuala Nerus while awaiting further arrangements.

items.title: 70,195 undocumented migrants detained in 10 months
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: A total of 70,195 undocumented migrants were detained in 11,808 enforcement operations conducted by the Immigration Department nationwide between Jan 1 and Oct 31. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said 155,498 people were inspected during the same period, while 328,744 registered under the Migrant Repatriation Programme 2.0. Zakaria said the department continued to take enforcement action against foreigners who breached immigration regulations, including overstaying, misusing passes or staying in the country without valid documents.

items.title: Retiree loses RM80,000 in WhatsApp investment scam
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: A 63-year-old retiree lost RM80,000 after falling victim to a non-existent online investment scheme promoted through WhatsApp. District police chief assistant commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the victim joined the scheme earlier this month after being introduced to it by an acquaintance. He said the victim was lured by promises of substantial returns within a short period.

items.title: Police hunt depot worker after colleague gunned down in Penang
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 15 — A man was shot dead, believed to have been killed by a colleague, at an oil storage depot in Bukit Tengah here yesterday. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng, when contacted by Bernama yesterday, confirmed the incident and said the suspect fled the scene after the shooting, with police actively searching for him. — Bernama

items.title: GKB sets record for largest number of children joining gut health programme
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A large number of children took part in a gut health awareness programme organised by GK Bio International Sdn Bhd (GKB), earning the company a place in the Malaysia Book of Records. The achievement was recognised under the category 'Largest Children Participation in Gut Health Awareness Programme'. HANDS-ON LEARNING Through interactive learning stations, children were introduced to the importance of maintaining good digestive health, making balanced food choices and drinking sufficient water every day.

items.title: MBPP culls 2,782 pigeons, crows in October
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) culled 2,782 pigeons and crows last month to curb pest nuisances and maintain public hygiene. MBPP said 1,035 pigeons were captured while 1,747 crows were culled during ongoing population control operations. In 2025, MBPP culled 17,750 crows and captured 10,171 pigeons.

items.title: Rauf to be sworn in as Melaka chief minister today
items.summary: MELAKA: Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh is expected to be sworn in as chief minister today. BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured enough seats to form the state government in yesterday's 16th Melaka state election. The BN-PN cooperation secured 24 of the 28 state seats contested, giving it a two-thirds majority in the state assembly.

items.title: Refugees, online scams among Dewan Rakyat focus next week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Rohingya refugees, cybercrime, haze and public health, including youth mental health, are among the issues expected to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat next week. According to the Order Paper published on Parliament's official website, Lim Lip Eng (PH-Kepong) will ask the Home Ministry for the latest number of Rohingya refugees in Malaysia and how many were repatriated to Myanmar this year. Datuk Muhammad Bakhtiar Wan Chik (PH-Balik Pulau) will ask the home minister to outline the government's long-term mechanisms for managing Rohingya refugees still in Malaysia following the suspension of third-country resettlement efforts.

items.title: More than 12,500 receive RM20.2m in Socso payouts under round-the-clock protection scheme
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Nov 15 — The Social Security Organisation (Socso) has disbursed RM20.23 million in benefits under the Non-Occupational Accident Scheme (Lindung 24 Jam) to contributors and their dependants as of Oct 31. Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan said the amount involved 12,582 eligible contributors and dependants who received various income-replacement benefits under Lindung 24 Jam to ensure their socioeconomic well-being in times of adversity. “A total of 373 recipients from Sabah received benefits amounting to more than RM481,000.

items.title: Malaysian Pacific Industries set to ride Infineon's AI power semiconductor growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd (MPI) is well-positioned to benefit from growing demand for advanced power semiconductor packaging, supported by the strong growth outlook of German chipmaker Infineon Technologies AG. The growth was driven by accelerating AI infrastructure investments, production capacity expansion and higher power semiconductor content per AI server. Infineon expects its combined AI and conventional data centre power revenue to reach nearly €4 billion in FY27.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin confers state honours on 218 recipients
items.summary: Also present were Raja Permaisuri Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, Raja Muda of Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa and Raja Di-Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzulkarnain Sultan Idris. Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad was also present. Anis Rizana, a former Customs Department director-general, will receive the Darjah Seri Paduka Mahkota Perak, which carries the title Datuk Seri.

items.title: From RM4.67m to RM1,000, KL’s historic Chinese Assembly Hall wins 99-year lease, says Hannah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — The government has approved a 99-year lease renewal for the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH), with the land premium fixed at a nominal RM1,000, a significant reduction from the earlier estimated premium of approximately RM4.67 million. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, in a Facebook post today, said the decision reflects the Madani government’s commitment to safeguarding Kuala Lumpur’s historical landmarks and ensuring that institutions of heritage significance can continue to serve future generations. She said the nominal premium was approved following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s commitment to give special consideration to the preservation of the historic building, after visiting the hall during a Chinese New Year celebration on February 17.

items.title: Bersama hit hardest as 26 candidates lose Melaka election deposits
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — A total of 26 candidates forfeited their election deposits after failing to secure at least one-eighth of the total votes counted in the 16th Melaka state election. Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) recorded the highest number of candidates losing their deposits, with 15 of its 16 candidates failing to secure the minimum number of votes required. Meanwhile, Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate Datuk Rais Yasin secured the largest winning majority of 16,214 votes in Sungai Udang, defeating the Bersatu and Bersama candidates, who obtained 2,103 and 1,322 votes respectively.

items.title: Hybrids make gains in US auto market amid high gasoline prices
items.summary: NEW YORK: Electric vehicle growth has hit a speed bump in the United States, but hybrid autos are gaining market share thanks to the jump in fuel prices due to the Iran war. Honda, a long-time rival to US hybrid market leader Toyota, announced this week $3 billion to build a new hybrid plant in Ohio and add capacity at plants in two other states. Nissan, which is launching its first significant hybrid product for the US market this fall, realized its absence in the category was denting sales, said Ponz Pandikuthira, a senior vice president at Nissan Americas.

items.title: Iraq PM sacks nine officials over alleged oil smuggling in pro-Iran group stronghold
items.summary: BAGHDAD: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi dismissed nine officials on Saturday, following an investigation into allegations of oil smuggling in the Jurf al-Sakher area, a stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataeb Hizbollah group. Zaidi, who came to power with US blessing, had launched earlier this week a probe into oil smuggling in the Jurf al-Sakher area – a stronghold of Kataeb Hizbollah, which Washington designates a terrorist organisation – in Babylon province, south of Baghdad. Washington has accused Iraqi armed groups of involvement in oil smuggling.

items.title: SpaceX catches Starship for first time after return from orbit
items.summary: STARBASE: SpaceX has caught the upper stage of its giant Starship rocket system for the first time after it returned to Earth on Saturday after a test flight into space, German Press Agency (dpa) reported. About 20 hours after launch, the Starship returned to the Starbase spaceport in southern Texas, where mechanical arms on the launch tower caught it. The upper stage, also called Starship, entered Earth's orbit shortly after separating from the booster and deployed satellites for SpaceX's internet service Starlink.

items.title: US diesel below US$6 a gallon at 2-month low on easing tensions, weaker demand
items.summary: NEW YORK: US diesel prices fell below US$6 a gallon on average on Saturday after two months above that threshold, retreating from record highs as easing geopolitical tensions and seasonal demand weakness reduce pressure on fuel markets. The national average retail diesel price was US$5.998 on Saturday, according to fuel price tracker GasBuddy. Diesel topped at US$6 a gallon on September 10 and hit a record US$6.519 on September 22.

items.title: Evacuation centres empty slowly in Selangor while Perak flood toll rises
items.summary: In SELANGOR, 1,493 victims from 398 families remain sheltered at seven PPS in Kuala Selangor, down from 1,511 victims from 405 families yesterday evening. According to InfoBencana portal of Social Welfare Department (JKM), the PPS at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Parit Mahang is housing the highest number of victims at 433, followed by SK Dato’ Maharaja Lela (391), Sekolah Rendah Agama (SRA) Bukit Kuching (303), the Bukit Kuching Tengah Community Hall (131), and Kafa Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (114). Meanwhile, in PERAK, the number of flood victims in the Hilir Perak district has risen to 293 people from 85 families, compared to 227 people from 66 families yesterday evening.

items.title: Macron’s first Malaysia visit promises fresh momentum from AI to defence
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — French President Emmanuel Macron will undertake an official visit to Malaysia on Nov 16 and 17, marking his first trip to the country. The Malaysia visit will follow Macron’s state visit to Cambodia from Nov 14 to 16, where he is expected to focus on strengthening bilateral relations, particularly in economic affairs, culture and healthcare. The French Presidency described Macron’s upcoming visit as “a new step” in bilateral relations.

items.title: A comprehensive silver economy strategy is needed
items.summary: LETTER: By 2030, Malaysia will have entered the ranks of ageing societies, with nearly five million people aged 60 and above. Ageing is discussed principally in terms of pension liabilities, healthcare expenditure, dependency ratios and the financial burden on families. The emerging silver economy - the goods, services, technologies and infrastructure serving older people - is becoming one of the world's most consequential economic frontiers.

items.title: Malaysian social enterprise among 3 winners of 2026 APEC BCG award
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian women-led social enterprise Kloth Circularity has emerged as one of three winners of the 2026 APEC Bio-Circular-Green (BCG) Award, in recognition of its efforts to transform discarded textiles into economic opportunities while empowering underserved communities. Kloth Circularity was recognised alongside two other small businesses from Hong Kong, China and Indonesia for their innovative approaches to converting food, agricultural and textile waste into economic opportunities while supporting local communities. Kloth Circularity co-founder Sarah Kedah said the enterprise hoped its journey would demonstrate how circularity could create livelihoods, strengthen local value chains and generate economic opportunities.

items.title: Asean pushes for faster operationalisation of haze control hub
items.summary: MANILA: Asean foreign ministers are seeking to fast-track the establishment of a regional coordination centre for transboundary haze control, the Philippine News Agency (PNA) reported. The renewed call was made during the Asean Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Pasay City on Saturday amid growing concerns over severe haze pollution that recently affected several Southeast Asian countries. The regional bloc adopted the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution in 2002 to prevent and monitor transboundary haze pollution caused by land or forest fires.

items.title: Anwar congratulates BN on Melaka win, urges focus on people’s welfare
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Barisan Nasional (BN) on the mandate given by the people of Melaka. He expressed hope that the trust placed in BN would be discharged with full responsibility for the well-being of the state and its people. In the 16th Melaka State Election today, BN won 21 of the 28 seats to secure a two-thirds majority, while PH took four seats.

items.title: Ringgit seen remaining soft against US dollar next week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit is expected to remain soft against the US dollar next week as the greenback remains well supported by expectations of further interest rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve (Fed). Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the greenback is expected to maintain its strength amid the Fed's hawkish monetary policy stance. Mohd Afzanizam expects the ringgit to trade between RM4.07 and RM4.10 against the US dollar next week.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia seen to consolidate as bargain hunting emerges
items.summary: On the index board, the FBM Emas Index slid 228.58 points to 11,736.89, the FBM Top 100 Index decreased 226.80 points to 11,571.65, and the FBM Emas Shariah Index trimmed 143.09 points to 11,679.68. The FBM ACE Index slipped 177.10 points to 5,063.14 and the FBM Mid 70 Index tumbled 237.55 points to 16,783.33. Weekly turnover narrowed to 11.59 billion units worth RM7.70 billion from 15.49 billion units worth RM14.43 billion in the previous week.

items.title: At 34, Kerk becomes Melaka’s youngest winner as Ab Rauf, 65, prevails
items.summary: Kerk polled 14,078 votes in a four-cornered contest for the Ayer Keroh state seat, defeating Perikatan Nasional (PN) candidate Gan Peng Lam (8,474 votes), Muhammad Muhaimin Lau Abdullah of Bersama (1,932 votes), and Mohd Hamnaim Mohamad of Bersatu (1,077 votes). Meanwhile, Ab Rauf retained the Tanjung Bidara state seat after securing 10,079 votes to defeat PH candidate Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri, who garnered 1,464 votes in a straight fight. Jalil (1,315 votes) to win with a majority of 7,857 votes.

items.title: Zelenskyy: US floated land-for-Nato deal in talks on ending Ukraine war
items.summary: KYIV: Washington suggested Kyiv cede land to Moscow in exchange for joining Nato, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in comments released Saturday, saying his country's relationship with the Western alliance is "back on the agenda." Moscow has pounded Ukraine in the run-up to winter, with Russian President Vladimir Putin showing no sign of backing down. Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?'

items.title: Packed Asean Summit schedule for Anwar in Manila
items.summary: MANILA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has a full schedule at the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits today, with the Myanmar crisis and South China Sea tensions expected to dominate discussions. Anwar is accompanied by Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. Later today, the prime minister will join fellow Asean leaders in separate meetings with representatives of the Asean Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA), the Asean Business Advisory Council (Asean-BAC) and Asean youth.

items.title: Health Ministry reassures patients after cyber breach targets file-sharing platform
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — All major operational systems, as well as the Ministry of Health’s (MOH) healthcare and patient treatment services, remain unaffected and are operating as usual following a cybersecurity incident detected on Thursday (Nov 12). The ministry said the incident was limited to unauthorised access to a support file storage and sharing platform at one of its facilities. “An initial investigation by MOH’s Computer Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT) found that the incident did not involve the encryption of the ministry’s main databases,” the statement said.

items.title: Italy fines Meta US$880mil over access to users' photos without consent
items.summary: MILAN: Italian regulators fined Facebook parent company Meta 805 million euros (US$880 million) for accessing users' photos without their "specific" consent, the country's data protection authority said on Saturday. Through the Facebook application for Android devices, Meta accessed photographs, videos and related metadata belonging to Italian users "without obtaining specific consent and without properly informing them", the authority said in a statement. Meta said it would appeal the decision.

items.title: Three tankers catch fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
items.summary: DUBAI: Iran's navy said three oil tankers caught fire on Saturday after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported. One tanker hit a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz on Saturday morning, while two others struck mines later in the day. "Two violating tankers ... were attempting to slip through a prohibited route in the Strait of Hormuz when they hit naval mines, exploded, and burst into flames," Iran's IRNA news agency quoted the Revolutionary Guards Navy as saying about the evening incident.

items.title: Global powers converge on Manila as Asean summit kicks off
items.summary: MANILA: A key regional summit opens on Sunday in Manila, with Southeast Asian heads of state facing questions on trade, security and an ongoing energy crisis while playing host to a who's who of global leaders. Brazil's recently re-elected Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, meanwhile, is set to attend a plenary session of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) on Sunday, while Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will sign a new defence pact with host country the Philippines. Hopes of achieving a so-called Code of Conduct in the disputed South China Sea between Asean states and China during Manila's year in the chair, meanwhile, have flagged.

items.title: US flight chaos traced to botched copper wire upgrade: Trump administration
items.summary: NEW YORK: Weary travellers braced for more flight disruptions Saturday as service resumed at US airports after an hours-long stoppage that the Trump administration blamed on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines. Lisa Beraid, 48, who works for an insurance company, told AFP as she waited for a flight Saturday morning at New York's La Guardia airport. By early afternoon, tracking website FlightAware had recorded at least 5,000 canceled flights for Saturday.

items.title: Penang puzzled by protests as most 'Sore Thumb' demands met
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government is puzzled by protests over the Tanjung Bungah Seaside Pocket Park, saying that nearly all residents' demands have been accommodated. Executive councillor Zairil Khir Johari said discussions involving the developer, Penang Island City Council, technical agencies and resident representatives had been underway since December 2025. Zairil said during the latest engagement on Oct 27, the developer agreed to integrate key community requests into the blueprint, including two public access points, native coastal planting and sufficient parking bays.

items.title: 'Sore Thumb' standoff tests Penang govt's handling of public objections
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The standoff between Tanjung Bungah residents and the Penang government over the "Sore Thumb" promontory will be a test of the state government's ability to manage public objections, said a non-governmental organisation. "The residents have been persistent, self-initiated and proactive in presenting reasonable, low-impact proposals for a public park that cost the government almost nothing," said Teh. Teh said the community's push aligned with Sustainable Development Goal 11 (sustainable cities and communities), rejecting claims that residents were driven by a "not-in-my-backyard" mentality.

items.title: Tanjung Bungah residents vow to defend 'Sore Thumb' from development [WATCH]
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Tanjung Bungah residents have vowed to defend their coastal promontory — known as "Sore Thumb" — from destruction. Resident Oo Huei Ying said pushing retaining walls beyond the high-water mark would alter the seabed and trigger severe coastal erosion along the sensitive Tanjung Bungah coastline. "A coastal park should co-exist with nature, not destroy it," she said, criticising blueprints that shave down the promontory for concrete tracks, parking bays, and amphitheatre-style retaining walls.

items.title: Atmaca expected to boost navy logistics
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The selection of Turkiye's Roketsan Atmaca antiship missile system to replace the cancelled Naval Strike Missile (NSM) on the Royal Malaysian Navy's littoral combat ships (LCS) could improve logistical efficiency and strengthen the country's defence industry. Universiti Pertahanan Nasional Malaysia Centre for Defence and International Security Studies director Professor Dr Adam Leong said Atmaca was an excellent choice for the LCS, particularly as the same missile system would also equip the littoral mission ship batch 2 (LMS B2) vessels. Leong said using a common missile system across different naval platforms would improve supply chain management, training, maintenance and logistical support.

items.title: Melaka fallout: Three key takeaways from BN-PN’s commanding win
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) captured 24 of Melaka’s 28 seats in yesterday’s state election, marking the third state poll in four months where Pakatan Harapan (PH) has lost ground after Johor and Negeri Sembilan. BN-PAS formula delivers again Melaka is the second consecutive state election, following Negeri Sembilan, in which BN and PN jointly outperformed PH. Before polling day, analysts noted that the arrangement could consolidate Malay votes, ending the vote-splitting among Umno, PAS, and Bersatu since 2018 that previously allowed PH to win multi-cornered fights.

items.title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship 'catch'
items.summary: STARBASE: Elon Musk's SpaceX on Saturday carried out the first-ever recovery of a spaceship, pulling off a successful "catch" of its Starship vessel as it returned to its launch site after a day in orbit. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes," SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Until now SpaceX had captured returning booster rockets three times.

items.title: Eisenkot rejects Netanyahu's unity appeal, calls it political 'tricks'
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israel's caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday reiterated his calls for a national unity government with his opponent Gadi Eisenkot, who in turn dismissed the appeal as a ruse. A meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday "only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government" to guarantee Israel's security, Netanyahu said in a video statement, adding that such a government could "eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all." The outgoing prime minister warned against Eisenkot's plan to form a minority government, presented as a "national emergency government."

items.title: BN-PN sweep Melaka in 24-seat landslide, Pakatan reduced to just four urban seats
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) have stormed to an emphatic two-thirds supermajority in the Melaka state election, capturing a combined 24 of the 28 state assembly seats, according to unofficial results tonight. In a sweeping victory that consolidated the ruling coalition's regional dominance, BN triumphed in 21 constituencies on its own, matching its 2021 seat benchmark, while PN captured three seats. PH suffered major political casualties across the state, losing former chief minister Adly in his Bukit Katil backyard to PN's Ridzuan Sarif.

items.title: Zahid confirms Ab Rauf as Melaka CM after BN-PN supermajority win
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) will nominate incumbent Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh to continue leading the Melaka government following their two-thirds majority in the 16th state election tonight. BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the letter of appointment for Ab Rauf would be submitted to Melaka Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam tonight. Unofficial results as of 9.20 pm showed BN and PN winning 24 of the 28 seats in the Melaka State Legislative Assembly.

items.title: ‘Much to explain and reflect upon’: Pakatan accepts Melaka election setback, says state chief
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has accepted the outcome of the Melaka state election and respects the people’s mandate despite winning only four of the 24 state assembly seats it contested, according to unofficial results. Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the coalition would use the results to assess its performance and strengthen efforts to regain public confidence. Adly said the results would also be brought before the PH Presidential Council for a comprehensive review, taking into account previous state election outcomes, including those in Johor and Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: Tok Mat says South China Sea code talks nearly 90pc complete, Malaysia pushing for deal by this year
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 14 — Nearly 90 per cent of the proposed Code of Conduct (COC) in the South China Sea has been agreed upon by Asean and China, with Malaysia optimistic that negotiations can be concluded soon. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said negotiations were in their final stage, although several outstanding issues still required political decisions. He said certain sensitive terms and provisions also needed mutual agreement among the countries involved.

items.title: George Town slashing video circulating online is week-old, man has been jailed, say police
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 14 — The suspect involved in the incident where a man was slashed with a knife in front of Sekolah Kebangsaan Batu Lancang here, as seen in the viral video of the incident on social media today, had already been arrested by the police the day after the incident. The police detected a video of the incident that went viral on social media today. The incident occurred on November 4 and a 30-year-old man had been arrested.

items.title: Anwar lands in Manila for Asean summit before brief dash back to meet Macron
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived here tonight for the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, with a packed diplomatic schedule that will see him return briefly to Malaysia to receive French President Emmanuel Macron before flying back to Manila. He was received by Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, Foreign Ministry Secretary-General Tan Sri Amran Mohamed Zin, and Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Datuk Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino Anthony. Tomorrow, Anwar is scheduled to attend the 49th Asean Summit Plenary and Retreat sessions, followed by engagements with the Asean Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA), Asean Business Advisory Council (Asean-BAC) and Asean youth representatives.

items.title: Police yet to receive further instructions on Shuhaily’s return from border control agency, says IGP
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) Director-General Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain continues to perform his duties as usual as no further instructions have been issued regarding his position. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the police had yet to receive any further instructions on whether Mohd Shuhaily would be returned to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM). “As I have explained before, Datuk Seri Shuhaily is a police officer who is serving a two-year contract as AKPS Director-General.

items.title: Police refer 32 Melaka election cases to AGC, including alleged seditious speeches
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Police have submitted 32 investigation papers related to the 16th Melaka State Election to the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) and are now awaiting further instructions. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said 42 police reports were received during the 14-day campaign period, on issues including the tearing down and burning of flags, as well as speeches by several individuals alleged to have contained seditious elements. The 16th Melaka State Election involves 28 state assembly seats.

items.title: Learn from Indonesia, tighten export monitoring to stop under-invoicing, say industry players
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Stricter monitoring of commodity exports is needed to curb under-invoicing, a practice in which exporters declare lower cargo values or quantities than what they actually ship, potentially causing losses in government revenue, maritime industry players said. Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said Indonesia’s move to set up a centralised agency to monitor major commodity exports should remind Malaysia to review how effective its own export monitoring systems are. Jeyenderan said Malaysia already had various electronic systems and government agencies responsible for monitoring export declarations, permits and supporting documents.

items.title: No disruption to border control agency after director-general’s transfer, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: LUMUT, Nov 14 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) continues to operate as usual nationwide, unaffected by the decision to return its director-general to his parent organisation, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM). That is not how it should be,” he told reporters after officiating the Madani Kita Programme (PMK) and the 2026 handover ceremony for the People’s Volunteer Corps’ (Rela) Kampung Angkat Madani (Madani Adopted Village) and Sekolah Angkat Madani (Madani Adopted School) initiatives at Kampung Sungai Tiram here today. On October 29, the Home Ministry decided that AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain would return to duty with the PDRM.

items.title: Equal access to house arrest? That’s not Home Ministry’s call, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: LUMUT, Nov 14 — The Home Ministry acts solely as the implementing agency for the Pardons Board’s decisions on a prisoner’s sentence, including house arrest. Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the ministry was not in a position to comment further on calls from various quarters regarding eligibility for house arrest, as pardon petitions fall outside its jurisdiction. Whether the sentence is reduced, set aside, or the person is released or placed under house arrest, our job is to implement it,” he told reporters.

items.title: 2026 Melaka State Election: Zahid thanks voters for BN-PN’s decisive 24-seat win
items.summary: If the claim holds, BN and PN together have taken all but four seats, which would leave Pakatan Harapan (PH) with just four, consistent with the seat-by-seat figures reported earlier, which showed PH holding only its urban seats of Kesidang, Ayer Keroh, Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir. PH has conceded the results. Of the 24 seats declared so far, BN has taken 19, Pakatan Harapan (PH) four and Perikatan Nasional (PN) one.

items.title: Melaka turnout hits EC’s 70pc target 50 minutes before polls close
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Voter turnout for the Melaka state election reached the 70 per cent targeted by the Election Commision (EC) by 5.10pm today, ahead of polls closing at 6pm. Serkam continued to lead with a turnout of 79.08 per cent, followed by Ayer Molek at 78.57 per cent, Tanjung Bidara at 75.94 per cent and Sungai Rambai at 75.83 per cent shortly after 5pm. This is followed by Kota Laksamana at 62.62 per cent, Sungai Udang at 64.46 per cent, Ayer Keroh at 65.29 per cent and Kesidang at 65.64 per cent.

items.title: Wedding day meets polling day as Melaka newlyweds cast votes in traditional red attire
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Nov 14 — A newlywed couple made their wedding day even more memorable by taking time to cast their votes in the 16th Melaka state election today, arriving at the polling centre in their traditional red wedding attire. Yau Wei Ming, 31, and his wife Chan Jia Lin, 27, headed to Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Machap Baru here after their wedding ceremony at a temple. Yau Wei Ming, 31, and his wife Chan Jia Lin, 27, pose for a photograph after voting in the 16th Melaka state election at SJKC Machap Baru in Melaka, November 14, 2026.

items.title: Seven impact marks, metal pellets found: Police probe suspected shooting at Sarikei business premises
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 14 — Police are investigating a suspected shooting incident after a business premises’ metal shutter was found with seven impact marks along Jalan Repok, Sarikei. Sarikei District Police Chief Supt Aswandy Anis said the premises owner lodged a report at 8.30pm on November 13 after hearing seven impact sounds coming from the direction of the shop’s folding metal shutter. Aswandy said preliminary investigations found two fragments of suspected metal pellets on the walkway outside the premises.

items.title: Anwar says legacy debts like 1MDB pushed up Malaysia’s debt, cautions that corruption ruins nations
items.summary: Anwar said the government had steadily reduced its budget deficit since he became finance minister in 2022, cutting the gap between spending and revenue from about RM100 billion that year to around RM90 billion, RM80 billion and RM70 billion in the following years. “It increased because have to pay old debts — 1MDB debt, Felda debt, I have to pay RM980 million per year; Tabung Haji debt, RM10 billion have to pay,” he said. The gap between government expenditure and revenue fell from RM100.84 billion in 2022 to RM92.44 billion in 2023, RM80.9 billion in 2024 and RM76.6 billion in 2025, but is projected to rise to RM80.5 billion this year before easing to around RM79 billion next year.

items.title: PM: Cyber, intrusion and terror threats top Malaysia’s security agenda as attacks hit thousands monthly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Malaysia is currently facing thousands of cyber attack attempts every month, thereby demanding a faster and more robust level of preparedness from security forces in confronting new-millennium defence threats. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that the country’s security landscape is no longer focused solely on conventional military threats; instead, cyber attacks, system intrusions, and terrorist cell movements have become the most critical challenges today. Therefore, we must strengthen (our defence), and last week I met with the top leadership of the Malaysian Armed Forces (ATM) to discuss strengthening the cyber security unit within the Armed Forces,” he said.

items.title: Thunderstorms, strong winds to hit seven states, KL and Putrajaya until 6pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds across seven states, as well as the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, effective until 6pm today. In Perak, the affected areas include Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Perak Tengah, and Manjung. A similar warning has been issued for Selangor, covering Klang, Kuala Langat, Sepang, Petaling, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, and Gombak as well as Negeri Sembilan in Port Dickson.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB confirms withdrawing letter to Rulers, maintains status quo of Tunku Muhriz
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 14 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has confirmed the withdrawal of the contents of a letter submitted to the Malay Rulers dated September 17 as well as the position previously taken by members of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (MMK) and effectively maintains the status quo regarding the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. Also present were the Undang of Luak Rembau, Datuk Sedia Raja Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, and the Undang of Luak Jelebu, Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi. The letter states that Ismail, together with 10 members of the State Executive Council (Exco), has unanimously decided to retract the contents of a letter dated September 17.

items.title: Slowest seat in Melaka? A look at the Bandar Hilir vote
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Bandar Hilir recorded the lowest turnout among Melaka’s 28 state constituencies, at just under 56 per cent as of 4.30pm today. The seat has 23,042 registered voters, with women making up 52 per cent of voters and men 48 per cent. Chinese voters make up about 73 per cent of the electorate, followed by Malays at 12.9 per cent, Indians at 6.4 per cent and others at 6.8 per cent.
